summary.headline: TMB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 34.97% YoY to a record INR412 crores, with total business up 23% to INR1,21,715 crores.
summary.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported its strongest quarter on record: net profit of INR412 crores (up 34.97% YoY), NII up 32.01%, and operating profit of INR611 crores (up 48.22%). Total business grew 23%, driven by advances up 27.01% (gold-heavy, with agri at 40% of the book) and deposits up 19.71%, with term deposits up 20.73% and CASA down 2.95% QoQ as the bank prioritised resource mobilisation. Management raised FY27 guidance for deposits, advances and total business by 2 percentage points each, and cut its cost-to-income guidance, while stating that ECL transition provisioning (INR276 crores set aside so far) will be phased in. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 0.69% and NNPA at 0.17%.

segments.name: Agri (incl. gold loans)
segments.commentary: 40% of advances; yield raised to 10.54% from 9.75%, which management attributes to deliberate gold loan repricing. Gold loan portfolio yield is 10.58%; management says the book can absorb about a 20% fall in gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: 28% of advances; YoY growth of 20.09% (earlier cited 14.89%), adding about INR500 crores per quarter. Yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 25% of advances. Home loans are declining but the decline is arrested; vehicle loans grew 25.7%. Retail shows a QoQ decline, which management partly attributes to migration from retail to agri gold loans.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 5.62% of advances; grew 6.69% YoY. Unsecured exposure is 10 bps of the book, with NPA of about INR56 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 CASA growth guidance of 17-18% reiterated; management expects CASA to recover from Q2 with 60 branch openings planned this year (6 opened in Q1).
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 18% from 16%; advances growth guidance raised to 21-22% from 20%; total business growth guidance raised to 20% from 18%.
NIM guidance: management expects to be well past 4% for the year versus the earlier 3.90% guide. ROA now expected to be well above 2% versus the earlier 1.9% guide.
ROE guidance revised to 15% (stated as a revised guidance). GNPA to stay below 1%.
Cost-to-income: earlier 46-47% range; management says it is revising this downwards by about 2 percentage points, after Q1 at 39.10%.

ECL: INR324 crores additional provision requirement at 30 June 2026; with INR250 crores COVID contingency provision and INR26 crores added in Q1, INR276 crores is set aside. No further provisions planned in Q2; phasing over 4-5 years permitted by RBI, with the bank aiming to complete it earlier.
FY27 IT budget of around INR280 crores; cybersecurity about 10% of this, with management signalling it will not be a constraint on spending.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 628 after 6 additions in Q1 (3 in Tamil Nadu, 3 outside); 171 branches are outside Tamil Nadu. Plan to open 60 branches in FY27 versus 44 in FY26.
IT spend of about INR280 crores in FY27: infrastructure 21%, new software acquisition and enhancement about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35% (as stated).
Business per employee INR23.75 crores; profit per employee INR32.12 lakh; 325 new employees recruited in Q1.
CD ratio 88.97% against a stated maximum of 99% on the bank's net worth; management expects term deposit focus to moderate CD ratio gains.
demand_pricing: Management expects gold loan growth to slow in H2 FY27 as gold prices stabilise around $4,000 per ounce; growth will be driven by tonnage and new customers rather than price.
Gold loan LTV: average 56.98%; consumption loans capped at 85% (principal plus accrued interest); agri gold loans have no LTV cap. Gold loans are 6-month or 1-year bullet structures, not EMI.
Gold loan share of advances is 46.97% (the transcript corrected 47.82%), with an informal internal cap of 50%.
Retail growth to come from vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and home loans (8-10% growth targeted for FY27) and LAP. MSME is targeted to grow 21-22%, combined with gold loans.
MSME to be grown through a hybrid CGTMSE-plus-collateral model; CGTMSE described as one of the ways to grow, not the main route.

financial_highlights.change: up 48.22% YoY; up from INR522 crores QoQ
CASA balance up 16.94% YoY, down 2.95% QoQ
GNPA down 53 bps YoY; NNPA down 16 bps YoY

qa_highlights.question: Digant Haria (GreenEdge Wealth) asked for FY27 guidance on loan growth, margins, ROA and ROE.
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the April guidance structure but raised it: deposits 16% to 18%, advances 20% to 21-22%, total business 18% to 20%, CASA 17-18% reiterated, NIM well past 4% (vs 3.90%), ROA well over 2% (vs 1.9%), ROE revised to 15%, GNPA below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Digant Haria asked when MSME and other retail would pick up, given the quarter was gold-heavy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME (YoY growth now above 20% vs 14.89% earlier, about INR500 crores added per quarter) as the lever to fill the gap as gold loan growth slows in H2 FY27 with gold prices stabilising near $4,000 an ounce.

qa_highlights.question: Laksh (Share India Securities) asked for MSME growth guidance and whether El Nino or the war had affected the book.
qa_highlights.answer: No specific MSME guidance yet; management said it would come back after the quarter, but expects growth well above the 20%-plus number put on the table. No stress seen so far from El Nino or the war, based on cash-flow studies and customer outreach.

qa_highlights.question: Parth (360 ONE Capital) asked what drove the QoQ rise in SMA 0, 1 and 2, and the divergent agri and MSME yields.
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan portfolio at-risk-one-day rose by roughly INR100-150 crores, now being contained by a corrective mechanism. Agri yield rose to 10.54% from 9.75% through deliberate gold loan repricing; MSME yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Parth asked about the Enforcement Directorate order on the foreign-investor shares and whether they are now free of encumbrance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was too early to comment; the bank is not party to the case between the ED and the investors. It has engaged a top legal firm to advise on the order, and the ED can still appeal.

qa_highlights.question: Parth asked why the retail portfolio declined QoQ.
qa_highlights.answer: Vincent M D said vehicle loans grew 25.7%, home loan decline has been arrested and is roughly at its 2025 level, and the bank expects home loans to grow 8-10% in FY27. Salee S. Nair attributed part of the QoQ retail decline to migration from retail gold loans to agri gold loans.

qa_highlights.question: Arvind (Sundaram Alternates) asked about MSME slippages and non-gold retail growth drivers.
qa_highlights.answer: The INR37 crore MSME slippage relates to only 2 accounts and is expected to be resolved in Q2. Gross NPA is INR160.35 crores vs INR202.34 crores in June 2025. Growth focus is home loans, vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and LAP.

qa_highlights.question: Vinith Jain (Siddhi Capital) asked about FY27 IT spend and ECL phasing.
qa_highlights.answer: IT budget is about INR280 crores: infrastructure 21%, software about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35%. ECL: INR276 crores set aside (INR250 crores COVID contingency plus INR26 crores in Q1) against INR324 crores required; no further provision planned in the current quarter, with completion targeted in FY28 and possibly earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vinith Jain asked whether there is an internal ceiling on the gold loan share, now 46.97% (corrected from 47.82%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management has an informal internal cap of 50% on the gold loan share. It expects the share to rise slightly but not significantly, and wants non-gold segments to grow in tandem.

qa_highlights.question: Nishit Shah (ViSolitech) asked whether CGTMSE is a route to grow MSME and whether a sub-40% cost-to-income ratio is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: CGTMSE is one route, used as a hybrid with collateral as skin in the game, not the main strategy. Management had earlier guided 46-47% cost-to-income, now revised down by about 2 percentage points; the sub-40% Q1 print included one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co) asked how the gold loan tonnage strategy differs from today and whether operating profit can hold near INR611 crores.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is shifting from price-led to tonnage and new customers, with branch advertising and gold loans delivered in under 10 minutes. On sustaining profit, management said MSME at a 10%-plus yield and other segments would support profit growth; it deferred a direct answer to the Q2 call.

risks_watch: Gold loan growth slowdown in H2 FY27 as gold prices stabilise near $4,000 per ounce; the bank says growth will need to come from tonnage and new customers. Gold loans are about 47% of advances against an informal 50% cap.
SMA 0/1/2 rose QoQ, driven by a INR100-150 crore uptick in gold loans at risk; management says it is under control but gave no figure. Watch the Q2 SMA trend.
ECL transition: INR324 crores required, INR276 crores set aside; RBI allows phasing over 4-5 years. Q2 provisioning and any trigger-based top-up need monitoring.

CASA ratio fell to 26.16% (down 2.95% QoQ) as term deposits were prioritised; management expects CASA to recover from Q2 with 60 branch openings planned for FY27 (6 done in Q1). Yield on advances and cost of deposits are key to NIM.

Enforcement Directorate show cause matters: penalty cut to INR3.4 crores with INR13.60 crores expected in Q2; SCN 2 adjudication pending; ED may appeal the order that dismissed confiscation of foreign-investor shares.
Cost-to-income at 39.10% in Q1 against the earlier 46-47% guide, now revised down by about 2 percentage points; management described the Q1 result as partly one-off.
key_quotes: We have delivered as promised, we have exceeded the guidance as promised in the last con call in April.
So, the portfolios are going to go in different directions.
So it is going to be a tonnage game going forward.
We will defend a 46% to 47% of cost-to-income ratio.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter's delivery and the upgraded FY27 guidance, but cautious on gold loan growth in H2 and on MSME pricing. Evasive on MSME-specific guidance (deferred to after Q1 close), on the ED order's implications for the shares, and on whether operating profit can hold at INR611 crores.

adds.what: 60 branch openings planned in FY27 (6 opened in Q1; 628 branches total)

growth.why: Raised FY27 guidance for advances (21-22%), deposits (18%) and total business (20%), backed by 60 planned branch openings (vs 44 in FY26), though management flags gold loan growth slowing in H2.
